Challa Punugulu Recipe | Bullet Bonda Recipe | Dahi Bonda | Bullet Bajji with step-by-step photo and video recipe. Pakoda, bajji, and other deep-fried snack recipes are super popular across Indian cuisine. These are usually made with besan or corn flour, but you can also use other less common flours like wheat or maida. One simple, easy plain flour-based deep-fried bonda or Bajji is the challa Punugulu recipe from Andhra cuisine, known for its size and crispy taste.

This recipe strongly resembles my hometown’s popular goli baje recipe. The ingredients list is similar, but the size and shape differ. Goli baje has more ingredients, like dry coconut, herbs, and spices. Whereas in this recipe, it is topped with basic spices. The main difference is the size. These challa Punugulu, or Bullet Bajji, are tiny. So, when served in large numbers, they look very attractive and appetising. Typically, you may not need anything and can easily gulp these hot bajji, yet the freshly prepared coconut chutney makes it an ideal snack meal. I recommend you try this snack and let me know what you think.

In addition, some more tips, additional variants, and suggestions to make a perfect Challa Punugulu Recipe. First, the recipe is ideally made with maida (plain flour), which helps it come out round. However, you can also make these yummy snacks with wheat flour or a combination of both. I personally like the plain flour version, but if you want something healthier, you can use wheat flour. Second, beat the batter, then drop it into the hot oil. Use a small scoop and drop it in quickly to form a ball-like shape. Lastly, if you take time to drop them into the oil, try frying them in small batches.

About Challa Punugulu Snack

Challa Punugulu is a traditional South Indian snack that people enjoy for its miniature size and crunchy texture. These small, deep-fried pakodas make an ideal tea-time snack that everyone can enjoy. The recipe comes from the rich cooking traditions that define Andhra Pradesh and Telugu culinary practices. Challa Punugulu literally means small fritters that are soft inside and crisp outside. Each South Indian state has its own version of the dish, with different sizes and taste profiles. Different regions also call this snack by different names, depending on local traditions. Freshly fried punugulu often appear in roadside stalls and busy street food markets. The three chutneys, which include coconut chutney, green chutney, and spicy peanut chutney, function as perfect side dishes. These small fritters also make an excellent accompaniment to lunch and dinner.

The main ingredient in traditional Challa Punugulu is plain flour or maida, which gives it an authentic taste and texture. Wheat flour also works well for those who prefer an alternative version. Sour yoghurt plays an important role in developing the batter’s flavour and texture. The yoghurt provides a delightful tang that enhances the taste of every bite. Many people also know these bite-sized fritters as Bullet Bajji or Bullet Dahi Bonda. Street vendors prepare them fresh and serve them hot throughout the day. Each golden fritter delivers a light, crispy crust with a soft centre. This versatile snack pairs well with evening tea, festive gatherings, and family celebrations. Challa Punugulu remains one of the most popular Telugu snacks because people have loved it for many generations.

Fun Fact

The name “Bullet Bajji” became popular because these tiny, round fritters resemble small bullets. Many street food vendors prepare hundreds of Challa Punugulu every hour, making them one of the fastest-selling evening snacks in Andhra Pradesh.

Chef Tips for Challa Punugulu

Classical Challa Punugulu is a crispy Andhra-style tea-time snack with a soft and fluffy centre. These tiny Bullet Dahi Bondas taste delicious with coconut chutney, green chutney or peanut chutney.

  1. Sour Yoghurt: Use well-fermented sour yoghurt for the batter. It gives the punugulu their signature flavour and soft texture.
  2. Batter Consistency: Prepare a thick and smooth batter before frying. This helps the punugulu hold their round shape and puff up beautifully.
  3. Frying: Drop small portions of batter into medium-hot oil. Gentle frying cooks the inside evenly while creating a crisp golden crust.
  4. Toppings: Add chopped onions, curry leaves and green chillies at the final stage. Fresh ingredients keep the batter light and aromatic.
  5. Serving: Enjoy the punugulu hot and crispy. Pair them with coconut chutney, green chutney or peanut chutney for the best flavour.

FAQs

  1. What is Challa Punugulu made of?
    Challa Punugulu traditionally uses maida, sour yoghurt, spices and basic seasoning. The batter creates small fritters with a crisp outside and soft centre.
  2. Why do we use sour yoghurt in Challa Punugulu?
    Sour yoghurt gives the batter its signature tangy flavour and helps create a light texture. It also supports gentle fermentation in the batter before frying.
  3. Can I make Challa Punugulu with wheat flour?
    You can prepare Challa Punugulu with wheat flour for a different variation. Keep the batter thick so the fritters hold their shape while frying.
  4. What chutney goes well with Challa Punugulu?
    Coconut chutney, green chutney and peanut chutney pair well with Challa Punugulu. Serve the fritters hot with any fresh chutney for a complete teatime snack.
  5. How do I make Challa Punugulu crispy?
    Prepare a thick batter and fry small portions in properly heated oil. Keep the heat medium so the fritters cook evenly and develop a crisp exterior.

Recipe card for Challa Punugulu

Challa Punugulu Recipe | Bullet Dahi Bonda | Bullet Bajji

HEBBARS KITCHEN
Enjoy the unique taste of challa punugulu. Try this easy bonda recipe for a delightful snack with your favorite dip.
5 from 2 votes
Email Tweet Share
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Save RecipeSaved!
Prep Time 10 minutes mins
Cook Time 20 minutes mins
Resting Time 3 hours hrs
Total Time 3 hours hrs 30 minutes mins
Course Snack
Cuisine andhra
Servings 3 Servings
Calories 380 kcal

Ingredients
  

  • 2 cup maida
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp baking soda
  • ¾ cup curd
  • water, as required
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 3 chilli, finely chopped
  • 2 tbsp coriander, finely chopped
  • oil, for frying

Instructions
 

  • firstly, in a  large bowl take 2 cup maida, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp baking soda. mix well making sure everything is well combined.
  • now add ¾ cup curd. you can alternatively use buttermilk.
  • mix well with your hand in one direction. add water if required.
  • beat the batter making sure to incorporate air well.
  • now add 1 tsp cumin, 3 chilli and 2 tbsp coriander.
  • mix well making sure everything is well combined.
  • cover and rest for 3 hours for best results.
  • after 3 hours, mix the batter again.
  • now dip your hand in cold water and pinch a small ball sized batter.
  • drop it in hot oil keeping the flame on medium.
  • stir and fry uniformly on medium flame.
  • drain off the bajji once it turns golden brown and crisp.
  • finally, challa punugulu is ready to enjoy with coconut chutney.

How to Make Bullet Bonda with Step-by-step photos

  1. firstly, in a  large bowl take 2 cup maida, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp baking soda. mix well making sure everything is well combined.
  2. now add ¾ cup curd. you can alternatively use buttermilk.
  3. mix well with your hand in one direction. add water if required.
  4. beat the batter making sure to incorporate air well.
  5. now add 1 tsp cumin, 3 chilli and 2 tbsp coriander.
  6. mix well making sure everything is well combined.
  7. cover and rest for 3 hours for best results.
  8. after 3 hours, mix the batter again.
  9. now dip your hand in cold water and pinch a small ball sized batter.
  10. drop it in hot oil, keeping the flame on medium.
  11. stir and fry uniformly on medium flame.
  12. drain off the bajji once it turns golden brown and crisp.
  13. Finally, challa punugulu is ready to enjoy with coconut chutney.

Notes

  • First, add water little by little, as the batter may turn runny otherwise.
  • Also, resting the dough will help to make punugullu super soft and spongy.
  • Additionally, fry on medium flame; otherwise, the bonda will remain raw from inside.
  • Finally, challa punugulu recipe tastes great when served hot.
